mainTopic: Why כלי זכוכית (glass vessels) are compared to כלי מתכות (metal vessels) for טומאה, and where that comparison stops
overview: The גמרא has compared glass to כלי חרס because both are made from sand. So it asks why glass is not like כלי חרס in never becoming טמא from its outer side. A משנה lists only כלי חרס and כלי נתר as sharing those rules, so glass is different. The answer: broken glass can be melted and remade, like metal, so חכמים compared it to כלי מתכות. The גמרא then asks why remade glass does not regain its old impurity (טומאה ישנה) the way metal does. It answers that glass impurity and טומאה ישנה are both only דרבנן, and חכמים do not put one rabbinic rule on top of another. Finally it asks why flat glass vessels are pure when flat metal vessels are טמא from the תורה. The answer is that חכמים made a deliberate difference (a הכירא) so people would know glass impurity is only rabbinic and would not burn תרומה or קדשים because of it.

steps.title: If glass is like earthenware, it should not become impure from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the comparison of glass to כלי חרס. Since כלי חרס cannot become טמא from its outer side, glass should not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: They (glass vessels) should not become impure from their outer side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just compared glass to כלי חרס because both are made from sand. Now it points out a problem with that comparison: glass should then not become טמא from its outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כלי חרס has a special rule: it only becomes טמא through its inner airspace, never through its outer surface. If glass were fully like כלי חרס, it would follow the same rule. The next step will show that glass does not actually follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer side or back of a vessel

steps.confusionAlert: This עמוד starts in the middle of a סוגיא. The words 'they should not become impure' are about glass vessels. They come right after the גמרא compared glass to כלי חרס because both are made from sand.

phrases.english: They should not become impure from their outer side.
phrases.notes: This continues the comparison of glass to earthenware made on the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a logical consequence from the earlier comparison of glass to כלי חרס (stated on the previous עמוד).
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of glass to כלי חרס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If glass is fully like כלי חרס, it should share its special rule of not becoming impure from the outside.

steps.title: A משנה shows only natron and earthenware share the same impurity rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that lists only כלי חרס and כלי נתר as having identical impurity rules. This implies that other vessels, glass included, are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet why did we learn: Earthenware vessels and natron vessels have the same impurity rules. They become impure and make other things impure through their airspace. They become impure from their back, but not from their outer side. Breaking them purifies them. So only natron and earthenware vessels share these rules, but other things do not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to sharpen the question. The משנה names only כלי חרס and כלי נתר as following these rules, so glass must not follow them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the special rules of כלי חרס: impurity through the airspace, through a hollow 'back' (bottom), never from the outer side, and breaking purifies. The גמרא reads the list as exclusive: only these two materials work this way. So glass, which is not listed, really does become טמא from the outside, and we need to know why it differs from כלי חרס.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels made of natron, a mineral substance
The inner airspace of a vessel
The back or underside of a vessel that has a hollow
Yet why did we learn (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'אחוריהן' (their back) with 'גביהן' (their outer side). 'Back' means a hollow under the base that can hold things, so it is still a kind of airspace. 'Outer side' means the plain outside surface.

phrases.english: Yet why did we learn:
Earthenware vessels and natron vessels
their impurity is the same:
they become impure and make things impure through their airspace,
and they become impure from their back (hollow underside),
but they do not become impure from their outer side,
and breaking them makes them pure.
Natron vessels and earthenware vessels
are the ones whose impurity is the same,
but other things — no!
phrases.notes: This is how we learn that glass is left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source showing that glass is in fact treated differently from כלי חרס, which strengthens the question.
steps.raayaObject: Glass vessels do become impure from their outer side, unlike כלי חרס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (כלים 2:1) that lists only כלי חרס and כלי נתר as sharing these impurity rules

steps.title: Glass is likened to metal because broken glass can be remade
steps.stepSummary: Broken glass can be melted down and made into a new vessel, just like metal. So חכמים compared glass to כלי מתכות for this rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: since glass vessels can be repaired after breaking, חכמים made them like metal vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. Glass is like metal in one important way: when it breaks, it can be melted and reshaped. So for this rule, it follows metal and becomes טמא from its outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken כלי חרס is finished, but broken glass, like metal, can be recast into a new vessel. That shared feature led חכמים to give glass the metal rule: impurity from every side. Glass is still compared to כלי חרס in its origin, but here it follows metal.

phrases.english: They say:
since, when they break,
they can be repaired (melted and recast),
they made them like metal vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי, כֵּיוָן דְּכִי נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ יֵשׁ לָהֶם תַּקָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why glass becomes impure from the outside even though it was compared to כלי חרס.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second comparison: glass is also likened to metal, based on a shared feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Glass is fully like כלי חרס and should never be impure from its outside
steps.terutzMaskana: Because glass can be recast, חכמים gave it the metal rule of becoming impure from every side

steps.title: Then remade glass should regain its old impurity like metal
steps.stepSummary: If glass is like metal, a broken glass vessel that is remade should return to its old impurity (טומאה ישנה), just as metal does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, they should return to their old impurity like metal vessels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If glass is like metal, it should also follow metal's rule of טומאה ישנה. The next two steps bring the sources for this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Metal has a unique rule: a טמא metal vessel that broke and was then remade becomes טמא again with its old impurity. If glass is truly like metal, the same should happen to glass. The גמרא is testing how far the comparison goes.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (now that you said this)
Old impurity that comes back when a broken vessel is remade

phrases.english: But if so,
they should return to their old impurity
like metal vessels?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer by pushing the glass and metal comparison further.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of glass to כלי מתכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If glass is like metal, it should share metal's rule of טומאה ישנה, but the sources say it does not.

steps.title: The משנה on metal vessels returning to old impurity
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that metal vessels, flat and hollow alike, can become טמא. If broken they become pure, and if remade they return to their old impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Metal vessels, both flat ones and ones that hold things, are impure. If they broke, they became pure. If he remade them into vessels, they return to their old impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for metal's rule of טומאה ישנה. This sets up the comparison with glass in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details matter here. First, metal vessels become טמא even when flat (with no place to hold things). Second, remade metal returns to its old impurity. Both details will come up later in the סוגיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Their flat vessels (with no inner space)
They broke, so they became pure

phrases.english: As we learned: Metal vessels,
their flat ones and their receptacles are impure.
If they broke, they became pure.
If he went back and made vessels from them,
they return to their old impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the metal rule mentioned in the question.
steps.raayaObject: Metal vessels return to their old impurity when remade

steps.title: The משנה shows remade glass is impure only from now on
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about glass and similar materials teaches that remade vessels become impure only from now on. So glass does not return to its old impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whereas about glass vessels we learned: Wooden, leather, bone, and glass vessels: flat ones are pure and receptacles are impure. If they broke, they became pure. If he remade them into vessels, they can become impure from now on. From now on, yes; retroactively, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that glass does not follow metal's rule of טומאה ישנה. This completes the challenge from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says remade glass is impure only 'from now on', meaning it can become טמא in the future. The inference is that it does not regain its old impurity. That is exactly where glass differs from metal, so the question is why the comparison breaks down here.

keyTerms.meaning: From now on (only in the future)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that this same משנה also says flat glass vessels are pure. The גמרא will use that detail later, in step 8.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding glass vessels we learned:
Wooden vessels and leather vessels
and bone vessels and glass vessels:
their flat ones are pure,
and their receptacles are impure.
If they broke, they became pure.
If he went back and made vessels from them,
they can receive impurity from now on.
From now on, yes;
retroactively, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets glass against metal to complete the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of glass to metal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Metal returns to its old impurity but glass does not, so glass is not fully like metal.

steps.title: חכמים do not add a rabbinic impurity on top of a rabbinic impurity
steps.stepSummary: The impurity of glass is only דרבנן, and טומאה ישנה is also only דרבנן. חכמים applied טומאה ישנה only to vessels whose impurity is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The impurity of glass vessels is rabbinic, and old impurity is rabbinic. Where the impurity is from the תורה, חכמים added the old impurity. Where the impurity is rabbinic, חכמים did not add it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about טומאה ישנה. It explains that חכמים would not place one rabbinic rule on top of another rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Metal impurity is from the תורה, so חכמים added the extra rule of טומאה ישנה. Glass impurity is itself only a rabbinic decree. So חכמים did not stack the further decree of טומאה ישנה on it. The comparison to metal still holds; this is just an exception in how it is applied.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern in ש״ס: חכמים usually do not make a decree on top of another decree.

phrases.english: The impurity of glass vessels is rabbinic,
and old impurity is rabbinic.
Regarding impurity from the Torah,
the Rabbis imposed (old) impurity on it;
regarding rabbinic impurity,
the Rabbis did not impose (old) impurity on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between metal and glass regarding טומאה ישנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between Torah-level and rabbinic-level impurity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If glass is like metal, it should follow every metal rule, including טומאה ישנה
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה ישנה is a rabbinic addition that applies only to vessels whose impurity is דאורייתא

steps.title: Flat glass vessels should at least be impure like flat metal
steps.stepSummary: Even so, flat glass vessels should be טמא, since flat metal vessels are טמא from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their flat vessels, at least, should become impure, since flat metal vessels are impure by Torah law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the glass and metal comparison. Flat metal is טמא, so flat glass should be too, yet the משנה said flat glass is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer worked because טומאה ישנה is itself rabbinic. But the impurity of flat metal vessels is from the תורה. So when חכמים copied the metal rules onto glass, they should have copied this basic rule too. This 'stacking' excuse does not apply here.

phrases.english: Their flat vessels, at least, should become impure,
since flat metal vessels
are impure by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer about טומאה ישנה but raises a different difference between glass and metal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in the משנה that flat glass vessels are pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flat metal is impure from the תורה itself, so the 'no decree on a decree' answer does not explain why flat glass is pure.

steps.title: A deliberate sign so people do not burn תרומה and קדשים
steps.stepSummary: חכמים deliberately left flat glass vessels pure as a sign that glass impurity is only rabbinic. This way people will not burn תרומה or קדשים that touched glass.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים made a distinguishing sign in them, so that people would not burn תרומה and קדשים because of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question. Leaving flat glass pure was done on purpose, to remind people that glass impurity is not from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If glass followed metal in every way, people might think glass impurity is from the תורה. They might then burn תרומה or קדשים that touched it, which may only be burned for impurity from the תורה. The difference (a הכירא) protects these holy foods. They are instead left in doubt, not burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Glass is compared to כלי חרס in origin and to metal because it can be recast. But its impurity is only דרבנן. So it does not take on טומאה ישנה (no rabbinic decree on top of a rabbinic decree). Its flat vessels are pure, as a deliberate sign that keeps people from burning תרומה and קדשים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that חכמים sometimes shape a rule on purpose so that it does not look like Torah law. That protects against serious mistakes, like wrongly destroying holy food.

phrases.english: The Rabbis made a distinguishing sign with them,
so that people would not burn
terumah and sacred foods because of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why flat glass vessels are pure despite the comparison to metal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Glass should copy metal's Torah-level rule that flat vessels are impure
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים deliberately made glass differ so people would know its impurity is only rabbinic and would not burn תרומה or קדשים
